summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, morbid obesity, and a history of peripheral arterial disease was admitted for a worsening right heel ulcer with dry gangrene. Imaging confirmed severe atherosclerotic disease in the right lower extremity, with patent anterior tibial arteries but heavily calcified and narrowed posterior tibial and peroneal arteries, limiting blood flow. A known right femoral arteriovenous fistula was noted but not acutely problematic. She received IV vancomycin and oral ciprofloxacin initially, followed by wound debridement by podiatry. Blood cultures remained negative. Due to the severity of ischemia, vascular surgery recommended a below-knee amputation as the definitive treatment, but the patient opted for conservative management. She was transitioned to oral Bactrim for three weeks and discharged to extended care with close follow-up planned. Nephrology adjusted her mineral metabolism regimen, discontinuing sevelamer and calcitriol and initiating weekly high-dose vitamin D due to elevated PTH. Her warfarin, insulin, and other chronic medications were continued.
problems: Atherosclerosis of native arteries of the extremities with gangrene
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
